2. It may be mentioned that upon converting the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.645 Of 1994 the aforementioned Title Suit No. 65 of 2002 was registered. The petitioner before the High Court Division filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No.645 of 1994 before the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge impleading' the opposite party in the revisional application with the prayer for appointment of sole Arbitrator and the parties to the Miscellaneous case mutually having had agreed sole Arbitrator was appointed but at certain stage the petitioner before the High Court Division lost confidence in the sole Arbitrator and thereupon filed application for removal of the sole Arbitrator as well  as for appointment of new Arbitrator but before the disposal of the said application the sole Arbitrator appointed earlier filed award before: the. Court on July, 20, 1998. As against the award it was alleged that the sole Arbitrator with malafide intention did not file the award even after lapse of 10 months since the closing of the proceeding but filed the award on the day following the day of the filing of the application for his removal and for appointment of a new Arbitrator. After the filing of the award the opposite party in the Miscellaneous Case i.e. petitioner herein filed an application with the prayer to convert the Arbitration Miscellaneous case into a title suit and the prayer so made was allowed and thereupon Arbitration Miscellaneous Case Nb.645 of 1994 was converted into Title Suit No.65 of 2002. The Arbitration Miscellaneous case having' been, converted into a title suit the Respondent who was petitioner in, the Arbitration Miscellaneous case filed an application under order 23, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking withdrawal of the Title Suit' No.65 of 2002 and the said prayer was rejected on the ground that the award was filed by the sole Arbitrator. As against the order of the trial court rejecting the prayer for withdrawal of the suit the Respondent moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. 

 3. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party i.e. petitioner herein, could not satisfy the Court under what provision of law the trial Court on the prayer of the opposite party in the Arbitration Miscellaneous case converted the said Miscellaneous Case into title suit. The High Court Division further observed since after converting the Miscellaneous case into title suit the petitioner in the Miscellaneous case, figured  as plaintiff in the title suit and consequently the title suit being the suit of the plaintiff, the plaintiff was quite competent' to seek withdrawal of the suit under Order 23, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure at any stage and that being the provision of law the trial Court was in error in rejecting the prayer of the plaintiff for withdrawal of his suit, that trial Court erred in law in converting the Arbitration Miscellaneous case into a title suit and that there is no sanction of law authorizing the Court to convert the Arbitration Miscellaneous case filed with the prayer 'for appointment of the Arbitrator to convert the same into a regular title suit at the instance of the opposite party in 'the Arbitration Miscellaneous case. The High Court Division also observed that after the filing of the award by the Arbitrator in the Court the opposite party in the Miscellaneous case was required to approach the Court to register a regular suit, wherein petitioner would be the plaintiff, for making the award rule of the Court but instead of doing that resorted to 'a procedure which has no sanction of law. 

 4. The learned Advocate-on4ecord submits that the High Court Division committed serious error in making the Rule absolute and thereupon allowing the prayer for withdrawal of the suit and thereby causing serious prejudice to the petitioner. We are of the view reasoning’s on which the High Court Division set aside the order of the trial Court rejecting the prayer for withdrawal of the suit is legally sustainable. Since after filing of the award in the Court by the sole Arbitrator the petitioner was required to approach the Court for registering a regular title suit wherein petitioner would be the plaintiff, for making the award rule of the Court but instead of doing that the petitioner herein approached the Court to convert the Arbitration Miscellaneous case into a title suit and the Court allowed the said prayer although there is no legal sanction for the Court to convert the Arbitration Miscellaneous case into the title suit. It may be mentioned after conversion of the Arbitration Miscellaneous case into a title suit the Respondent was shown as the plaintiff of the so converted title suit This being the position the Respondent as plaintiff was competent to file an application under Order 23, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking withdrawal of the suit in which he is a plaintiff. The trial Court being quite unmindful of the said state of the matter and the provision of law rejected the prayer for withdrawal of the suit and consequently committed error which had legally been interfered by the High Court Division.
